questions.question: Write a note on the voltage generation in a battery.
questions.solution_html:
• A battery generates voltage through electrochemical reactions that occur in an electrochemical
  • cell. Each cell consists of two electrodes—an anode and a cathode immersed in an
  • electrolyte.At the anode, oxidation occurs, releasing electrons. These electrons flow through
  • an external circuit to the cathode, where reduction takes place by accepting electrons. This
  • movement of electrons constitutes an electric current, and the difference in electrical potential
  • between the two electrodes is the voltage of the battery
  • Eg : A dry cell generates voltage through a chemical reaction between its components. It
  • consists of a zinc outer casing (which acts as the anode) and a carbon rod surrounded by a
  • manganese dioxide paste (which acts as the cathode). The electrolyte paste, typically
  • ammonium chloride or zinc chloride, facilitates ion movement.When the circuit is connected
  • a chemical reaction occurs between the zinc and the electrolyte, releasing electrons at the
  • anode. These electrons travel through the external circuit to the carbon cathode, creating an
  • electric current. The potential difference between the anode and cathode determines the
  • voltage, typically around 1.5V for a standard dry cell.
  • (Any relevant three points/ explanation of working of any specific cell – (3marks))

questions.question: Compare Transfer Moulding and Compression Moulding.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare Transfer Moulding and Compression Moulding.
  • Transfer moulding is a process used to shape thermosetting materials by heating and pressing
  • them into a mould. It begins with the material being placed into a chamber separate from the
  • main cavity. When heat and pressure are applied, the softened material flows through channels
  • into the mould, ensuring a precise and even distribution. This technique is particularly
  • beneficial for producing complex shapes with embedded components, such as electronic parts.
  • It also offers better control over material flow, reducing defects like air pockets, but tends to
  • be more expensive due to additional equipment and material wastage.
  • Compression moulding, on the other hand, involves placing a pre-measured amount of
  • material directly into an open mould cavity, then closing the mould and applying heat and
  • pressure to shape it. This method is widely used for making strong, durable products like
  • automotive parts and electrical insulators. Unlike transfer moulding, compression moulding is
  • more cost-effective and requires simpler machinery, making it ideal for large-scale production.
  • However, it can sometimes lead to variations in thickness and may not be suitable for intricate
  • designs requiring fine details.
  • (Any three relevant points of both moulding – (3 marks))
questions.final_answer: (Any three relevant points of both moulding – )

questions.question: Describe the function and importance of a salt bridge in an electrochemical cell.
questions.solution_html:
• Salt bridge is usually an inverted U-tube filled with concentrated solution of inert
  • electrolytesGenerally salts like KCl, KNO3, and K2SO4 etc. are used. For the preparation of
  • salt bridge, gelatin or agar-agar is dissolved in a hot concentrated aqueous solution of an inert
  • electrolyte and solution thus formed is filled in the U-tube. On cooling the solution set in the
  • form of a gel in the U-tube. The ends of the U-tube are plugged with cotton wool as to minimize
  • diffusion effects.
  • Function of salt bridge: (a) It connects the solutions of two half cells and complete the cell
  • circuit. (b) It prevents transference or diffusion of the solutions from one half cell to the other.
  • (c) It keeps the solutions in the two half-cells, electrically neutral.
  •  Prevents Charge Buildup – In an electrochemical cell, oxidation occurs in the anode half
  • cell, releasing positive ions into the solution, while reduction takes place at the cathode
  • consuming positive ions. Without a salt bridge, an excess of charge would develop, disrupting
  • the reaction.
  •  Completes the Circuit – The salt bridge provides a pathway for the movement of ions
  • allowing the reaction to continue by enabling the flow of electric current between the
  • electrodes.
  •  Maintains Ion Balance – It contains an inert electrolyte (usually KCl or KNO₃), which
  • allows the free movement of cations and anions to counteract charge imbalances while
  • preventing unwanted side reactions.
  •  Prevents Direct Mixing – Unlike a porous partition, which physically separates the
  • solutions, the salt bridge keeps them from mixing directly while still allowing controlled ion
  • exchange.
  • (Definition with any two relevant points – (3 marks), functions – (4marks))
questions.final_answer: Option It connects the solutions of two half cells and complete the cell

questions.question: Describe the working of a lithium ion battery and its uses.
questions.solution_html:
• Working:A Lithium-ion battery works based on the reversible movement of lithium ions
  • between two electrodes through an electrolyte. It consists mainly of a graphite anode, a lithium
  • metal oxide cathode (such as LiCoO₂), an electrolyte (typically a lithium salt in an organic
  • solvent), and a separator. During discharge (when the battery is in use), lithium atoms in the
  • anode undergo oxidation and release electrons and lithium ions. The electrons travel through
  • the external circuit, providing electrical energy, while the lithium ions move through the
  • electrolyte to the cathode. At the cathode, these ions combine with electrons and undergo
  • reduction. During charging, an external power source forces the reverse process: lithium ions
  • move back from the cathode to the anode, and energy is stored in the battery. This continuous
  • intercalation and deintercalation of lithium ions between the electrodes enables repeated
  • charge–discharge cycles with high efficiency.((4 marks))
  • Uses: Lithium-ion batteries are widely used in modern technology due to their high energy
  • density, lightweight nature, and long cycle life. They are commonly found in portable
  • electronic devices such as smartphones, laptops, and tablets. They are also extensively used in
  • electric vehicles, renewable energy storage systems, power tools, and medical devices. Their
  • ability to provide reliable and rechargeable energy makes them essential in both consumer
  • electronics and large-scale energy applications.((3 marks))

questions.question: Explain the process of polymerization in the formation of thermoplastic and thermosetting polymers.
questions.solution_html:
• polymers.
  • Polymerization is the chemical process by which small molecules called monomers combine
  • to form large macromolecules (polymers), and the nature of this process determines whether a
  • material becomes a thermoplastic or a thermosetting polymer. In thermoplastic polymers
  • polymerization typically occurs through addition (chain-growth) or condensation (step-growth)
  • reactions that produce mostly linear or slightly branched chains without extensive cross
  • linking. In addition polymerization, unsaturated monomers (like ethylene) react by opening
  • their double bonds and linking together in a chain reaction, while in condensation
  • polymerization, monomers combine with the elimination of small molecules such as water or
  • methanol. Because these polymers have little or no cross-linking, the intermolecular forces
  • between chains are relatively weak, allowing the material to soften upon heating and harden
  • upon cooling repeatedly without significant chemical change.
  • In thermosetting polymers are formed through polymerization processes that create a highly
  • cross-linked, three-dimensional network structure. Initially, monomers or low molecular
  • weight prepolymers react (often through condensation or addition mechanisms) to form a
  • viscous or soft intermediate, which upon further heating or curing undergoes extensive cross
  • linking. This curing process forms strong covalent bonds between polymer chains, resulting in
  • a rigid, infusible, and insoluble structure. Once set, thermosetting polymers cannot be remelted
  • or reshaped because heating does not soften them but instead leads to decomposition. Thus, the
  • key difference lies in the degree of cross-linking formed during polymerization, which governs
  • the thermal and mechanical behavior of thermoplastics and thermosets. (Explanation of both
  • polymers – (7 marks))
questions.final_answer: polymers – )

questions.question: Describe the ultimate analysis of coal and how it differs from proximate analysis.
questions.solution_html:
• Ultimate analysis of coal is a detailed chemical analysis that determines the elemental
  • composition of coal, namely the percentages of carbon (C), hydrogen (H), nitrogen (N), sulfur
  • (S), and oxygen (O). Carbon and hydrogen are usually estimated by burning a known mass of
  • coal in oxygen and measuring the amounts of carbon dioxide and water formed. Nitrogen is
  • commonly determined by methods such as the Kjeldahl method, sulfur is estimated by
  • converting it into sulfate and measuring it, and oxygen is calculated by difference. This analysis
  • provides precise information about the chemical makeup of coal and is useful for calculating
  • calorific value, combustion requirements, and assessing environmental impact.
  • In contrast, proximate analysis is a simpler and quicker method that determines the physical
  • constituents of coal, namely moisture content, volatile matter, ash content, and fixed carbon. It
  • involves controlled heating of coal under specified conditions to measure weight loss and
  • residue. While proximate analysis gives a general idea about the fuel behavior during
  • combustion, ultimate analysis gives a more detailed and quantitative understanding of the
  • elemental composition. Thus, the main difference is that ultimate analysis deals with chemical
  • composition, whereas proximate analysis deals with physical components and combustion
  • characteristics.
  • (Ultimate analysis – (3.5 marks), Proximate analysis – (3.5 marks))
questions.final_answer: Option (c) , hydrogen (H), nitrogen (N), sulfur

  • automotive parts and electrical insulators. Unlike transfer moulding, compression moulding is

questions.question: Describe the function and importance of a salt bridge in an electrochemical cell.
questions.solution_html:
• Salt bridge is usually an inverted U-tube filled with concentrated solution of inert
  • electrolytesGenerally salts like KCl, KNO3, and K2SO4 etc. are used. For the preparation of
  • salt bridge, gelatin or agar-agar is dissolved in a hot concentrated aqueous solution of an inert
  • electrolyte and solution thus formed is filled in the U-tube. On cooling the solution set in the
  • form of a gel in the U-tube. The ends of the U-tube are plugged with cotton wool as to minimize
  • diffusion effects.
  • Function of salt bridge: (a) It connects the solutions of two half cells and complete the cell
  • circuit. (b) It prevents transference or diffusion of the solutions from one half cell to the other.
  • (c) It keeps the solutions in the two half-cells, electrically neutral.
  •  Prevents Charge Buildup – In an electrochemical cell, oxidation occurs in the anode half
  • cell, releasing positive ions into the solution, while reduction takes place at the cathode
  • consuming positive ions. Without a salt bridge, an excess of charge would develop, disrupting
  • the reaction.
  •  Completes the Circuit – The salt bridge provides a pathway for the movement of ions
  • allowing the reaction to continue by enabling the flow of electric current between the
  • electrodes.
  •  Maintains Ion Balance – It contains an inert electrolyte (usually KCl or KNO₃), which
  • allows the free movement of cations and anions to counteract charge imbalances while
  • preventing unwanted side reactions.
  •  Prevents Direct Mixing – Unlike a porous partition, which physically separates the
  • solutions, the salt bridge keeps them from mixing directly while still allowing controlled ion
  • exchange.

  • releases electrons to the external circuit.

  • from the external circuit.
  • Electrolyte: A chemical medium (liquid, solid, or gel) that allows the movement of ions
  • between the anode and cathode, enabling the electrochemical reaction.
  • Separator: A porous insulating material placed between the anode and cathode to prevent direct
  • contact (short circuit) while allowing ion flow.
  • Current collectors: Conductive materials (usually metals) that collect and transfer electrons
  • between the electrodes and the external circuit.

questions.question: Explain the plastic casting process
questions.solution_html:
• Plastic casting is a manufacturing process in which a liquid plastic material is poured into a
  • mould and allowed to solidify into the desired shape. The process starts with preparing a
  • suitable mould made of materials such as metal, silicone, or plaster. A liquid resin, usually a
  • thermosetting polymer like epoxy, polyester, or polyurethane, is then mixed with a curing
  • agent, along with pigments or fillers if required. This mixture is carefully poured into the mould
  • while avoiding air bubbles, sometimes using vacuum or pressure techniques to improve quality.
  • The mould is then left undisturbed for curing, during which a chemical reaction converts the
  • liquid into a solid plastic; this may occur at room temperature or require heating. After complete
  • hardening, the изделие is removed from the mould and finished by trimming or polishing if
  • necessary, making plastic casting a simple and effective method for producing complex shapes
  • with good surface finish. (Any three points – (3 marks))

questions.question: Analyze the role of carbon fibers in enhancing the mechanical properties of composite materials.
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze the role of carbon fibers in enhancing the mechanical properties of composite
  • materials.
  • Carbon nanofibers are nanoscale carbon-based fibers, typically with diameters ranging from
  • tens to hundreds of nano meters and lengths in the micro meter range, characterized by a high
  • aspect ratio, graphitic structure, and exceptional mechanical, thermal, and electrical properties.
  • Carbon fibers play a crucial role in enhancing the mechanical properties of composite materials
  • due to their high tensile strength, excellent stiffness, low density, and superior load-bearing
  • capability. When incorporated into a matrix such as epoxy, they act as the primary
  • reinforcement phase, carrying most of the applied stress and thereby significantly improving
  • the strength and rigidity of the composite while keeping it lightweight. These composites also
  • exhibit excellent fatigue and creep resistance, enabling them to withstand repeated and long
  • term loading without significant degradation. Their anisotropic nature allows engineers to tailor
  • mechanical properties by aligning fibers in specific directions according to load requirements
  • resulting in optimized structural performance. In addition to conventional carbon fibers, carbon
  • nanofibers have gained importance as advanced reinforcement materials due to their high
  • surface area and strong interfacial interaction with the matrix, which enhances stress transfer
  • and improves properties such as toughness, modulus, and crack resistance at the nanoscale.
  • Furthermore, both carbon fibers and carbon nanofibers contribute to thermal stability and
  • corrosion resistance, ensuring durability in harsh environments. However, despite these
  • advantages, carbon-based composites can be relatively expensive and may exhibit brittleness
  • and lower impact resistance. The incorporation of carbon fibers and carbon nanofibers leads to
  • high-performance composites with superior mechanical properties suitable for advanced
  • engineering applications.

questions.question: Describe the working of a lithium ion battery and its uses.
questions.solution_html:
• Working:A Lithium-ion battery works based on the reversible movement of lithium ions
  • between two electrodes through an electrolyte. It consists mainly of a graphite anode, a lithium
  • metal oxide cathode (such as LiCoO₂), an electrolyte (typically a lithium salt in an organic
  • solvent), and a separator. During discharge (when the battery is in use), lithium atoms in the
  • anode undergo oxidation and release electrons and lithium ions. The electrons travel through
  • the external circuit, providing electrical energy, while the lithium ions move through the
  • electrolyte to the cathode. At the cathode, these ions combine with electrons and undergo
  • reduction. During charging, an external power source forces the reverse process: lithium ions
  • move back from the cathode to the anode, and energy is stored in the battery. This continuous
  • intercalation and deintercalation of lithium ions between the electrodes enables repeated
  • charge–discharge cycles with high efficiency.((4 marks))
  • Uses: Lithium-ion batteries are widely used in modern technology due to their high energy
  • density, lightweight nature, and long cycle life. They are commonly found in portable
  • electronic devices such as smartphones, laptops, and tablets. They are also extensively used in
  • electric vehicles, renewable energy storage systems, power tools, and medical devices. Their
  • ability to provide reliable and rechargeable energy makes them essential in both consumer
  • electronics and large-scale energy applications.((3 marks))
questions.final_answer: electronics and large-scale energy applications.()

questions.question: Explain the process of polymerization in the formation of thermoplastic and thermosetting polymers.
questions.solution_html:
• polymers.
  • Polymerization is the chemical process by which small molecules called monomers combine
  • to form large macromolecules (polymers), and the nature of this process determines whether a
  • material becomes a thermoplastic or a thermosetting polymer. In thermoplastic polymers
  • polymerization typically occurs through addition (chain-growth) or condensation (step-growth)
  • reactions that produce mostly linear or slightly branched chains without extensive cross
  • linking. In addition polymerization, unsaturated monomers (like ethylene) react by opening
  • their double bonds and linking together in a chain reaction, while in condensation
  • polymerization, monomers combine with the elimination of small molecules such as water or
  • methanol. Because these polymers have little or no cross-linking, the intermolecular forces
  • between chains are relatively weak, allowing the material to soften upon heating and harden
  • upon cooling repeatedly without significant chemical change.
  • In thermosetting polymers are formed through polymerization processes that create a highly
  • cross-linked, three-dimensional network structure. Initially, monomers or low molecular
  • weight prepolymers react (often through condensation or addition mechanisms) to form a
  • viscous or soft intermediate, which upon further heating or curing undergoes extensive cross
  • linking. This curing process forms strong covalent bonds between polymer chains, resulting in
  • a rigid, infusible, and insoluble structure. Once set, thermosetting polymers cannot be remelted
  • or reshaped because heating does not soften them but instead leads to decomposition. Thus, the
  • key difference lies in the degree of cross-linking formed during polymerization, which governs
  • the thermal and mechanical behavior of thermoplastics and thermosets. (Explanation of both
  • polymers – (7 marks))
questions.final_answer: polymers – )

questions.question: Describe the ultimate analysis of coal and how it differs from proximate analysis.
questions.solution_html:
• Ultimate analysis of coal is a detailed chemical analysis that determines the elemental
  • composition of coal, namely the percentages of carbon (C), hydrogen (H), nitrogen (N), sulfur
  • (S), and oxygen (O). Carbon and hydrogen are usually estimated by burning a known mass of
  • coal in oxygen and measuring the amounts of carbon dioxide and water formed. Nitrogen is
  • commonly determined by methods such as the Kjeldahl method, sulfur is estimated by
  • converting it into sulfate and measuring it, and oxygen is calculated by difference. This analysis
  • provides precise information about the chemical makeup of coal and is useful for calculating
  • calorific value, combustion requirements, and assessing environmental impact.
  • In contrast, proximate analysis is a simpler and quicker method that determines the physical
  • constituents of coal, namely moisture content, volatile matter, ash content, and fixed carbon. It
  • involves controlled heating of coal under specified conditions to measure weight loss and
  • residue. While proximate analysis gives a general idea about the fuel behavior during
  • combustion, ultimate analysis gives a more detailed and quantitative understanding of the
  • elemental composition. Thus, the main difference is that ultimate analysis deals with chemical
  • composition, whereas proximate analysis deals with physical components and combustion
  • characteristics.
  • (Ultimate analysis – (3.5 marks), Proximate analysis – (3.5 marks))
questions.final_answer: Option (c) , hydrogen (H), nitrogen (N), sulfur
